## Design

### 2026-10-05 — Hi community. First, I went through a quick tutorial, since I'm more used to EasyEDA rsrsrs.

**6h**

Hi community. First, I went through a quick tutorial, since I'm more used to EasyEDA rsrsrs.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-10-05 at 21.53.50](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/efcdda4710348adb50829fa1d092cc1f3a1d302154af81cc67912caf317d9075.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-10-05 at 22.54.29](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/f64e75d0cb37b6ff8e0318711aebacf6ffbd88c1e7f292c720817681ae2bcb92.jpeg)

I started this session aiming to lay out the core components of my ESP32-S3 macropad. Initially, I made a mistake by selecting the bare ESP32-S3 SoC instead of the module. I realized my mistake and reorganized the layout to use the ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 module for easier soldering later.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-10-05 at 21.53.50](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/efcdda4710348adb50829fa1d092cc1f3a1d302154af81cc67912caf317d9075.jpeg)
Next, I tackled the power delivery, connecting a USB-C receptacle to an AMS1117-3.3 LDO. I thought just connecting VBUS and GND was enough, but I learned a crucial hardware lesson today: if someone uses a USB-C to USB-C cable (like a Mac charger), it won't provide 5V unless it detects a device! To solve this, I had to add two separate 5.1kΩ pull-down resistors to the CC1 and CC2 pins.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-10-05 at 21.54.15](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/545a13477a98ba9a4092b646bb48e4ba60000d2fd794dd3d2717ca728d2cb653.jpeg)
I also learned that voltage regulators are highly unstable without filters, so I added 10uF ceramic capacitors to the input and output of the LDO (I actually almost used a condenser microphone symbol by accident before fixing it!). To ensure the ESP32 boots properly, I wired a 10kΩ pull-up resistor and a 1uF capacitor to the EN pin.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-10-05 at 22.18.10](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/f3bc013efd4f3798a5e4f2e6376f69a2b08554b11dfced5f5a5679b5c8de1705.jpeg)
Finally, I started mapping the mechanical switches using Net Labels (IO1 to IO9) to keep the schematic clean and avoid having messy wires crossing everywhere.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-10-05 at 22.57.40](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/629ee4a60f91d0b9d73dbbe4831683d252723393d106654ae36645368918d0cd.jpeg)

![WhatsApp Image 2026-10-05 at 23.07.08](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/600e640abc2a702e7379e5e5a8a77cc5e0aee00e7cad367ecc28553d4d6e9af8.jpeg)

### 2026-10-06 — The journey of the past 5 hours has been one of pure dedication to hardware design. What started as an idea for a custom ESP32-S3 macropad began to take real shape in KiCad. The first major milestone

**5h**

The journey of the past 5 hours has been one of pure dedication to hardware design. What started as an idea for a custom ESP32-S3 macropad began to take real shape in KiCad. The first major milestone was the electrical schematic: integrating the microcontroller, mapping the OLED display, configuring the rotary encoder, and ensuring that the data communication for the LED cascade was perfect.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-10-06 at 07.45.08](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/5670261bd2ed4f7ca18d63d27b7ad34e71cf2b32685e5b9ce2ca7208df908070.jpeg)

![WhatsApp Image 2026-10-06 at 08.03.31](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/4a526305ccf3277fe423c0e0dd8046b0beb8123f70dc2d6a59a8ba52ff4c238d.jpeg)
When transitioning to the physical board design, I faced the classic footprint conflicts. I debugged and resolved each one of them with a clear goal in mind: to ensure that this is a genuinely open-source and easy-to-replicate project. To achieve this, I made a point of standardizing the selection with the industry's most universal components, ensuring compatibility with Cherry MX switches and common SMD resistors.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-10-06 at 08.28.27](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/d585ec5eb2239e27c78af305b55a3e43263445dadb88c3e406d99eb6d00d7b24.jpeg)

![WhatsApp Image 2026-10-06 at 08.16.28](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/bda1b8a7fa3836461ec1eeac2158bcb4efe989dee56a5f50431bc9d75660654f.jpeg)
The most satisfying moment was undoubtedly updating the PCB and successfully placing all the components in the editor without a single error. The logical foundation is solid and validated. The next step is organizing the physical layout of the panel and starting the track routing. The effort in electronics always pays off!

![WhatsApp Image 2026-10-06 at 08.45.14](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/3f7d30ca769ec1d16a37816a2586109a48a2dd22f6f2c2baecabbde5acd63b98.jpeg)
